source_caption: Before the Birkin became synonymous with luxury, there was Jane Birkin herself. This London-born actress and singer, who made France her home, transformed simplicity into something uniquely chic with her effortless style—combining jeans, a white shirt, and a worn-in blazer in a way only she could. In Agnès Varda’s 1988 film Jane B. par Agnès V., Jane Birkin opens the iconic bag named after her, revealing everyday items like notebooks, books, pens, and makeup. This scene beautifully encapsulates her intention for the Birkin: a functional bag that carries a life, not merely a status symbol. While the handbag bears her name, it is Jane’s enduring persona that remains truly indelible. Acknowledgments go out to the talented individuals who have captured these unforgettable moments.
